Property Price Modelling

Excel · regression · descriptive statistics · model comparison
Business question

Which property features drive sale price, and how accurately can price be predicted?

Approach

Profiled 2,005 transactions, then compared a full four-predictor model with a simpler refined model using R², RMSE, MAE, AIC and BIC.

Results
$940,094mean price (median $800,000)
+$507price per extra square foot
+$103,948per extra bathroom
R² = 0.62RMSE about $348,600
Takeaway

The refined model kept the same accuracy with one fewer predictor (lot size dropped) and a stronger F-statistic (1,082.7 vs 811.7). Beds show a negative effect (−$105,904) once size and baths are controlled for.

Retail Customer Behaviour: Hypothesis Testing in R

R · ggplot2 · chi-square · t-test · ANOVA · Tukey HSD · regression
Business question

How do customer gender, income and shopping frequency relate to store choice and satisfaction across 363 customers in 16 store locations?

Results
p = 0.0175gender and store location are associated (χ² = 48.5, df 30)
p = 0.128Bondi vs Newtown income: no significant gap (121.3k vs 93.0k)
p = 0.002income differs by shopping frequency (F = 5.03)
+33.0kweekly vs occasional shoppers’ income (p = 0.041)
+0.029satisfaction points per extra item; R² = 0.16
Takeaway

Weekly shoppers earn significantly more than daily (+22.6k) and occasional shoppers, which supports premium placement for weekly customers and promotions to win occasional ones. Item count predicts satisfaction, but weakly, so other drivers matter.

Retail Discount Impact: SQL

MySQL · window functions · data cleaning
Business question

What revenue would be lost if a 4% discount were applied to lower-value transactions, in Electronics only versus across all categories?

Approach

Removed rows with missing values, used PERCENT_RANK to find the 10th and 30th percentile transaction values ($51.85 to $105.98), then modelled revenue before and after the discount for both scenarios.

The query that answers it
-- 1. Transaction value thresholds (10th and 30th percentile)
SELECT
  MAX(CASE WHEN pct_rank <= 0.10 THEN TotalAmount END) AS p10_value,
  MAX(CASE WHEN pct_rank <= 0.30 THEN TotalAmount END) AS p30_value
FROM (
  SELECT TotalAmount,
         PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY TotalAmount) AS pct_rank
  FROM transactions
) AS ranked;

-- 2. Scenario A: 4% discount, Electronics only
SELECT 'Scenario A - Electronics Only' AS scenario,
  COUNT(*) AS affected_transactions,
  ROUND(SUM(TotalAmount), 2) AS original_revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(TotalAmount * 0.96), 2) AS revenue_after_discount,
  ROUND(SUM(TotalAmount) - SUM(TotalAmount * 0.96), 2) AS revenue_loss
FROM transactions
WHERE ProductCategory = 'Electronics'
  AND TotalAmount BETWEEN 51.85 AND 105.98;

-- 3. Scenario B: 4% discount, all categories
SELECT 'Scenario B - All Categories' AS scenario,
  COUNT(*) AS affected_transactions,
  ROUND(SUM(TotalAmount), 2) AS original_revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(TotalAmount * 0.96), 2) AS revenue_after_discount,
  ROUND(SUM(TotalAmount) - SUM(TotalAmount * 0.96), 2) AS revenue_loss
FROM transactions
WHERE TotalAmount BETWEEN 51.85 AND 105.98;

Superstore Sales Dashboard (Power BI)

Power BI · DAX · Power Query · data modelling
Business question

Which regions, categories and products drive revenue and profit, and how is monthly revenue trending?

Results
2.30Mtotal sales across 5K orders
286.40Ktotal profit
12.47%profit margin
+3.79%month-over-month revenue growth
Takeaway

Overall margin is healthy, but some sub-categories lose money: Tables sell 206,966 yet run a −8.56% margin (−17,725 profit), with Bookcases (−3.02%) and Supplies (−2.55%) also negative. Labels (44.42%) and Fasteners (31.40%) are the most profitable lines.

Discount & Profitability Dashboard (Tableau)

Tableau · KPI cards · calculated fields · discount tiers · geography
Business question

Do discounts help or hurt profit, and which regions and categories drive it?

Approach

Built a dashboard on 9,994 Superstore orders with discount tiers, running profit by tier, regional profit share, sales vs profit by sub-category, monthly sales trends and month-over-month KPI cards.

Results
−99.6Kprofit on orders with 41%+ discount (−77% margin)
+321.0Kprofit on orders with no discount (29.5% margin)
37.9%of profit comes from the West, then East at 32.0%
12.47%overall margin on 2.30M in sales
Takeaway

Heavy discounting destroys profit: orders discounted 41% or more lose about 99.6K, and medium discounts (21 to 40%) lose another 35.8K, while no-discount orders earn 321.0K. Capping discounts below 20% would protect margin.
